questions: Does the starting block count as a path (the zero-move path), and is it included in the total number of possible paths?
Are paths considered distinct based on the sequence of moves (i.e., order of x and y steps) or only based on the set of visited blocks?
Is the starting block chosen from all blocks satisfying the conditions, and does each starting block contribute separately to the total count?
Are moves restricted to only positive x and positive y directions, or can he move in any combination as long as each step is in one of those two directions?
If he moves to a block that is outside the defined region (L,R,D,U), is that move invalid even if the coordinates are integers?
Does the path have to be simple (no revisiting blocks), or can he revisit blocks during the operation?
Is the number of operations bounded by anything other than the block constraints, or can he move arbitrarily many times as long as he stays on blocks?
Are paths considered distinct if they have different lengths but visit the same blocks in the same order?
